title: [ROCm][Perf] Tune Triton W4A16 dense GEMM tiles for gfx90a (104 CUs)
body:
## Purpose — why this change exists

The Triton W4A16 dense GEMM's tile table routes gfx90a into its **MI300
branch, tuned for 304 CUs**. An MI210 has 104. At decode widths that starves
the card: with `BLOCK_N=64`, a narrow-N layer launches only **80–96
workgroups onto 104 CUs** — fewer than one per CU — while the SMs sit idle.
Shrinking `BLOCK_N` for the gfx90a narrow shapes raises that to 320–384
workgroups and lets the card actually fill.

This is the same class of issue as any large-SI tile table being reused for
a small-SI part: the dispatch is legal, so nothing fails — the kernel just
runs at a fraction of the achievable rate and nobody notices.

title: [Core][KV Connector] Bounded early prefetch for waiting requests
body:
## Summary

Fixes #41784

When the running queue saturates the per-step token budget, the 
waiting-queue scheduling loop never executes, so KV connectors with 
async disk/network loads (e.g. LMCache) never start their lookups 
until the running queue drains. By then the GPU is already idle 
waiting on the just-started lookup, wasting hundreds of milliseconds 
per request and cascading under load.

This PR adds an optional `_early_prefetch_waiting_kv` pass that runs 
at the top of each `schedule()` call, before the running queue is 
processed, and hints the KV connector to start async lookups for 
waiting requests. This lets connectors kick off async loads while the 
GPU is still busy, hiding disk latency behind ongoing GPU work.

title: [HiSparse][1/n] Add Dynamic HiSparse Residency to Preserve Small-Batch Decode Performance
body:
## Motivation

This PR adds dynamic HiSparse residency to avoid unnecessary performance regression in small-batch decode.

Before this change, once a request entered HiSparse, its KV cache was backed up to host and the device-side KV was still cut down to `device_buffer_size`. This static behavior is useful when HBM is under pressure, but it is too aggressive for small batches. In small-batch scenarios, there is often enough spare HBM to keep the full device KV resident, so forcing every HiSparse request into the shortened device-buffer mode makes decode unnecessarily slower.

With dynamic HiSparse, a request still gets host backup after entering HiSparse, but its full device KV is preserved by default. title: [MM] Add Triton kernel for mm_input_normal.
body: ## Purpose `mm_input_norm` is a memory-bandwidth-bound operator: one multiply-add per element, so runtime is dominated by DRAM traffic. This PR adds a Triton fusion kernel that performs the whole per-channel affine transform in a single pass, replacing the eager path that materialized an fp32 intermediate. The Triton fused kernel is **significantly faster** than the eager, `BatchNorm1d`, and `torch.compile` baselines on the same workload, because it reads the input once and writes the output once — no intermediate DRAM round-trip. https://github.com/noooop/snippet/tree/main/kernel_bench/mm_input_normal This basically saturates my local 4090's VRAM bandwidth ～850GB/s.

title: [AMD] greedy LM-head AG+argmax shortcut with EAGLE compatibility
body:
## Motivation

This PR adds an AMD/HIP-only fast path for greedy decode when the LM head is tensor-parallel sharded. Instead of materializing full-vocab logits via TP all-gather and then running `torch.argmax`, each rank computes its local `max/argmax`, all-gathers only `(max_value, local_index)` pairs, and reconstructs the global token id.

The route is opt-in via:

```bash
SGLANG_AITER_AG_ARGMAX_SHORTCUT=1
SGLANG_AITER_AG_ARGMAX_SHORTCUT_MIN_M=2
```

Non-HIP platforms are explicitly gated out and continue using the existing full-logits path.
